question_text: A 42-year-old man presents to a free dermatology clinic, complaining of itchy skin over the past several days. He has no insurance and lives in a homeless shelter. The patient has no significant medical history. Physical evaluation reveals 2 mm erythematous papules and vesicles on his back and groin, with linear excoriation marks. Careful observation of his hands reveals serpiginous, grayish, threadlike elevations in the superficial epidermis, ranging from 3–9 mm in length in the webbing between several digits. What should be the suggested treatment in this case?
